name: Adonispill

lead: Adonispill is a term used on looksmax.org for a mindset centred on the "Adonis" ideal: a male physique with wide shoulders, a tight waist and low body fat. The suffix "-pill" follows the usual community pattern of naming a worldview that someone adopts.

The appearance payoff is proportion. Lifting to widen the shoulders and back while keeping the waist lean changes the shoulder-to-waist ratio, which published research has linked to ratings of male attractiveness. The word itself is informal and has no formal definition or studies of its own.

paras: Followers describe it as a package of habits: resistance training aimed at the upper body, body-fat control, posture, grooming and general discipline. The term is often used in motivational posts that contrast an idealised "Adonis" routine with a less disciplined one.
No physical risks attach to the idea itself. As with any physique ideal, forum members sometimes pair it with aggressive dieting or enhancement, which carry their own risks covered in other articles.

chain: Train shoulders and back, keep body fat low
angle.text: The framework gives people a concrete physique target. Following it through resistance training and leanness widens the shoulder-to-waist ratio, the proportion highlighted in research on male attractiveness.

lead: Adonispill is a piece of looksmaxxing slang. It combines "Adonis", the figure from Greek myth long used as shorthand for an ideally handsome man, with the community suffix "-pill" that marks a worldview or framework someone takes on. On looksmax.org the word appears in threads that hold up an idealised male physique and lifestyle as a target [1].

The physical side of the idea is proportion. Wikipedia's article on waist-to-hip ratio notes a study in which waist-to-chest ratio was the largest determinant of male attractiveness, ahead of BMI and waist-to-hip ratio [2]. Members who use the term generally point to this kind of V-shaped silhouette: broad shoulders and back tapering to a lean waist.

Adonispill is not a measured index or a clinical concept. It has no published definition, and no study has tested it by name. It is documented here as a piece of community vocabulary and a motivational framework.

Wide shoulders, narrow waist, lean frame

paras: Posts using the term describe an idealised man whose body, habits and confidence are treated as the model to imitate. Typical threads are motivational or humorous in tone, and some are explicitly self-mocking, with posters adding disclaimers about irony [1].

The shared physical picture is the classic V-taper. Researchers have examined proportion in male attractiveness, and one study cited on Wikipedia found waist-to-chest ratio to be the largest determinant of male attractiveness [2].
Like other "-pill" terms, it works as an identity label as much as a plan. Posters invoke it to encourage training consistency, and others use it ironically [1].
No studies found. Research on male body proportions and attractiveness exists more broadly, for example the waist-to-chest ratio finding noted above [2].

lore.intro: Threads on looksmax.org use the term for an aspirational physique-and-lifestyle ideal, sometimes sincerely and sometimes as a joke [1].

claims.claim: Following the "Adonis" ideal leads to a more attractive physique
